text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish paper workers' union should stay in line and support a comprehensive pay deal in the autumn round of collective bargaining, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.
- Finland's Green party elected MP Satu Hassi, licenciate of techology, their new leader after a close race between Hassi and the former chairman, Tuija Brax.
- A weekend conference of the Swedish People's Party voted against building new nuclear power capacity. @
- Pirate copies of branded products are still being shipped to Russia via Finland, National Board of Customs says.
- Finland's soccer team beat Azerbaijan 3-0 in their group three World Cup qualifier on Sunday.

- Finnish state-owned alcohol company Alko's Primalco unit plans to launch massive marketing effort on behalf of Finlandia Vodka, spending millions in the U.S. to secure its position among the top brand vodkas. @
- Small and medium-sized companies and mechanical forestry industry will be new focuses of study at the Pellervo Economic Research Institute, the institute's managing director said.
- Rooting out economic crime requires competent prosecutors and up-to-date legislation, new state prosecutor Matti Kuusimaki says.
- Members of the Swedish People's Party relected Minister for European Affairs Ole Norrback as their leader. @
- Retail groups in Finland are expanding into the 'super-kiosk' business, as old restrictions on opening hours of shops under 100 square metres have been removed.
- Finland could apply for membership of NATO, the Conservative party says, sharpening its stance.
